name: Horus House
subtitle: Party Base of Operations
body:
A three-story narrow rowhouse in the Hive Ward, near the ward border. Horus Lanternholder owned it. Now the party does.

Ground floor: kitchen, common room, a workbench. Second floor: two bedrooms. Third floor: Horus's study and a roof access hatch. Basement: trapdoor under a kitchen rug, crates of supplies and magical items including the bag of withholding.

The house is in decent repair. Horus kept it functional rather than comfortable. There is food in the kitchen. There is a lock on the front door. The lock is better than the neighborhood suggests.

callout.label: NEW HAVEN PORTAL
callout.text: The house connects to New Haven via a portal in the study. Four conditions required: roof, invited host, shared meal, spoken welcome. As Horus's household, the party satisfies conditions 1–3 automatically when one member cooks from house supplies. They must still speak the welcome.

name: The Mortuary
subtitle: Dustmen Headquarters, Sigil Corpse Disposal
body:
The Mortuary is Sigil's official body-processing facility. Every corpse in Sigil comes here, by law. The Dustmen maintain it, staff it, and manage the paperwork that follows every death in the city.

It is large, gray, and smells of preservation chemicals. The staff are professional and slightly offputting. The queue for disposal during high-tension periods can be several days long. The Dustmen do not rush.

The party's first visit follows the Session One combat at Horus House. Three Rusted Bell bodies, no witnesses except the party. The Dustmen require: cause of death, names if known, and the disposal fee (5 gp per body for standard processing). They do not ask difficult questions. They have seen worse.

name: The Gray Ledger (Shop Front)
subtitle: Money-Lending Shop, Gray Ledger Front Operation
body:
A tidy shopfront on a Hive Ward commercial corridor. Sign reads "The Gray Ledger — Loans, Accounts, Exchange." Clean windows, a bell on the door, a queue of ward residents waiting for service.

Wex works the counter. He is pleasant, efficient, and knows exactly what the posted rates are and nothing else. The counting room is one floor up, accessed by a door behind the counter that requires a key Wex does not have.

The shop is legitimate in the way that a front operation is legitimate: the loans are real, the payments are collected, the paperwork is filed. The accounting behind the accounting is where the interesting material is.

callout.label: INVESTIGATION
callout.text: The counting room holds the evidence for Clue 3. DC 15 Perception or Investigation to notice the inconsistency in the posted ledger. DC 20 to access the back records. Drusine is gone before the party gets here.

name: The Ninefold Headquarters
subtitle: Ninefold HQ and Ward Portal Site
body:
A converted warehouse in the Hive Ward's interior, claimed by the Ninefold as their central operation. Salt runs meetings from a back office. The main floor is used for goods transit and labor placement — legitimate businesses that the protection operation runs alongside.

One of the nine corridors the Ninefold controls runs directly to a portal site in the warehouse's loading dock. The portal key is a specific knot pattern tied in rope. Salt knows the key. His lieutenants do not.

The warehouse is not comfortable and not designed to be. It is functional: a place where work gets done.
